title: Negatives and Questions Quiz 1
description: Use do, does, am, is and are to make present tense negatives and questions.
instructions: Negatives and Questions: Present simple and present continuous.
Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Does she works in a bank?
Do she work in a bank?
Does she work in a bank?
Is she work in a bank?
questions.explanation: Does takes the -s, so the main verb goes back to the base form: Does she work. Watch out: does + works is the most common slip.

questions.question: Make the negative: 'He plays tennis on Sundays.'
options: He doesn't play tennis on Sundays.
He doesn't plays tennis on Sundays.
He don't play tennis on Sundays.
He doesn't playing tennis on Sundays.
questions.explanation: Present simple negative: does not + base verb. Watch out: the -s of plays disappears because doesn't carries it.

questions.question: {{1}} they {{2}} (watch) the match now?
questions.explanation: Now points to the present continuous, so the question uses Are + subject + verb-ing. Watch out: do is not added when the helper is already be.

questions.question: She {{1}} (not / like) coffee.
questions.explanation: Present simple negative with she: does not + base verb. Watch out: not likes, because does already carries the -s.

questions.question: 'Do you be tired?' is correct.
questions.explanation: With be as the main verb the question is Are you tired? Watch out: be is its own helper and never takes do.

questions.question: Which question is correct?
questions.explanation: Present continuous question: Are + subject + verb-ing. Watch out: do / does never goes before a verb-ing form.

questions.question: Choose the correct helper to make each sentence negative.
questions.explanation: The subject and the tense decide the helper. Watch out: I takes am not, and plural subjects in the present simple take do not.

questions.question: Match each sentence with its question.
questions.explanation: Find the helper first, then put it before the subject. Watch out: He is a pilot has be, so there is no do or does.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order to make a question.
questions.explanation: The helper Are comes first, then the subject, then the -ing verb. Watch out: the subject you goes between Are and listening.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
options: I don't going to school today.
questions.explanation: Three sentences use the right helper and the right verb form. Watch out: the other two keep an -s after does or add don't before a verb-ing form.

questions.question: In which sentence does the negative need NO do or does?
questions.explanation: She is happy becomes She isn't happy, because be is its own helper. Watch out: all the other verbs need don't or doesn't.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: Does she likes pizza?
questions.explanation: After does the verb is in the base form: Does she like pizza? Watch out: the -s belongs to does, not to the verb.
